# dsh-plugin-updater

A plugin updater for DSH. It finds the plugins in your profile that were
installed from GitHub, comp

ares each one's installed version with the
`version` in `package.json` on the latest commit of its r

epository's `main`
branch, and updates them — one at a time or all at once.

Everything lives inside dsh's own **Plugins** page (the sidebar's Plugins
panel), in its existing **
Installed plugins** section. There is no extra tab.

- **Under the "Installed plugins" heading**:
- **Check for updates** re-runs the check; the time of

the last check is
shown beside it.
- **Update all (N)** updates every plugin with an update availabl

e, one
after another. A failure doesn't stop the others.
- Lines for a check error, the restart noti

ce, and the empty or
unsupported state.
- **After an update** (single or Update all), a snackbar at

the bottom of the
window reports how many were updated and how many failed, then hides after
a few s

econds.
- **On each GitHub plugin's card** that has something to say:
- an *Update available · x.y.z

* tag (or *updating*, *update failed*,
*update check failed*) and *pinned to …* when installed with
ck or an update failed.

Up-to-date and non-GitHub cards are left exactly as dsh draws them.
- **On an outdated plugin's own

page**: an *Update available · x.y.z* badge
beside its title and an **Update** button among its head

actions.
- **At startup** a check runs once in the background. When it finds updates,
a toast says

how many; **View** opens the Plugins page and scrolls to
Installed plugins. The toast hides by itsel

f after 3 seconds; a thin bar
along its bottom shrinks from right to left as the time runs out.
## How it works

- **Which plugins.** Bundles whose install source is a GitHub repository:
`github:owner/repo`, `git+

https://github.com/owner/repo(.git)`,
`https://github.com/owner/repo`, `git+ssh://git@github.com/…`

or
`git@github.com:owner/repo`, each with or without `#ref`. Registry, local
(`link:` / `file:`), ta

rball and other git hosts are ignored.
- **Which version.** It asks `api.github.com` for the head co

mmit of `main`,
then reads `package.json` at that exact commit from
`raw.githubusercontent.com`. Ver

sions are compared with SemVer precedence;
only a strictly greater `main` version counts as an updat

e.
- **Updating.** dsh's plugin manager has no update action, so the updater
does what its UI does:

remove the bundle, then install
`github:owner/repo#main` with the same enabled/disabled state. If th

e
install fails, the previous commit (from `pnpm-lock.yaml`) is reinstalled.
When dsh says the chang

e needs a restart, a notice under the Installed plugins heading says so.
- **Pinned plugins.** A plu

gin installed with `#tag`, `#branch` or `#commit`
is still compared with `main`. Updating it asks fi

rst, because it then
tracks `main`. The question is an in-app dialog built from dsh's own
`Modal` an

d `Button` (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-primitives`), with
**Cancel** and **Update**; only a dsh tha

t does not share those falls back
to the browser's `confirm`.
- **Updating the updater itself.** Whe

n the updater is installed from GitHub
and `main` is newer, its card and its page show **Update Plug

in Updater**:
an outline button with a refresh icon, unlike the solid **Update** of other
plugins. I

t always asks first, pinned or not, and **Update all** never
includes it.
- It never uninstalls itse

lf (removing a bundle stops it first). It runs
`pnpm add github:owner/repo#main` in place through ds

h's
`runPluginCommand`, under the same profile lock as the plugin manager.
- If that fails, `package

.json` and `pnpm-lock.yaml` are put back and the
current version keeps running.
- On success it writ

es `<dshHome>/storages/plugin-updater/self-update.json`
and asks dsh to load the new version live. W

hen dsh can't, the Installed

quests/hour unauthenticated limit. |

## Install

Needs **dsh 0.2 or later** (the `pluginManager` service and the native
Plugins page). Tested with 0.

sh 0.2 or later** (the `pluginManager` service and the native
Plugins page). Tested with 0.2.1-rc.2.

The `desktop` profile is managed by the Electron app: add the plugin from the
app's plugin manager a

s a local folder (a `link:` dependency, like the other
`@local/*` bundles). For a `web` profile:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Caveats

- **Public GitHub repos and `main` only.** Private repos, repositories whose
branch is not `main` (e

.g. `master`) and subfolder installs (`#path:`)
show as *unknown*.
- **Rate limit.** Without a token

, GitHub allows 60 API requests per hour.
When it is hit, the updater falls back to `raw…/main/packa

ge.json` (which
the CDN can serve a few minutes stale) and shows no SHA.
- **Blocked build scripts.*

* pnpm 10+ blocks a git dependency's `prepare`
script until it is allowed in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` (

`allowBuilds`). Such
an update fails with the plugin manager's message; the updater never
approves b

uilds for you.
- **Version-based.** New commits that don't bump `version` aren't reported.
- **Self-

update relies on dsh internals.** It loads `runPluginCommand` from
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-plugin-manager/

operations` out of dsh's installation
(`profileContext.installAnchor`). On a dsh without it, the upd

ater's card
keeps the "uninstall and reinstall it" hint instead of the button.
- **Fragile Installed

-section hook.** The Installed plugins section and its
cards have no extension seat. A `shell.overla

y` entry watches the page and
mounts its controls next to `section[data-plugin-group="bundles"]` and

`li[data-plugin-package]` (selectors in `SEL` in `client.js`). A harness
update that changes that m

arkup may need a matching tweak; until then the
card controls just don't appear, and the detail-page

badge and button
(official seats) keep working.
